children: Our Bureau Bengaluru: Digital lending startup Fibe received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO) comprising fresh shares worth up to 750 crore and an offer for sale of 40.07 million shares by existing investors.

According to its draft red herring prospectus, Fibe's major investors including The Rise Fund of TPG, Norwest Venture Partners, Chiratae Ventures, Piramal Finance and Eight Roads Ventures will be selling shares as part of the public offering.

The Pune-based company plans to invest 562.6 crore from its proceeds from the IPO in subsidiary EarlySalary Services to augment the non-banking financial company's capital base and support onward lending. The remaining proceeds from the sale of fresh shares will be used for general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2015 by Akshay Mehrotra and Ashish Goyal, Fibe was previously known as EarlySalary. It started as a small-ticket, short-term personal loan provider and has since expanded into longer-tenure unsecured personal loans and purpose-linked financing across healthcare, education, insurance and other consumption categories.

The company, whose backers also include TR Capital and International Finance Corporation (IFC), has so far raised more than $250 million in equity, including secondary transactions. In December 2025, Fibe raised $35 million from IFC. Before that, it raised $90 million in June 2024 in a mix of primary and secondary capital from TR Capital, Trifecta Capital and Amara Partners, along with existing investors.

title: Digital Lender Fibe Gets Nod for 750-cr IPO
